results.result: Syndapin III KO mice show severe reduction of caveolae in muscle cells. TEM analyses of cardiomyocytes revealed that WT membranes showed about 2 caveolae/µm membrane stretch, while syndapin III KO mice displayed only 0.29 caveolae/µm (15% of WT). The density of cav3-marked deep invaginations was severely reduced in syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C32-C34, and C40 are well-supported by quantitative TEM data showing dramatic reduction in caveolar density. The measurements are specific, quantitative, and consistent across multiple analytical approaches (thin sections and freeze-fracture). Statistical significance is demonstrated (C34, Figure 2c).

results.result: Caveolin3 and CAVIN-1 protein levels remain unchanged at the plasma membrane in syndapin III KO cells despite severe reduction in caveolar invaginations. Western blot analyses and immunogold labeling showed that the overall anti-cav3 immunolabeling density at the plasma membrane and the density within cav3 clusters remained constant in syndapin III KO cells compared to WT.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C41-C42, C45-C46, C80-C81 are strongly supported by multiple independent methods: quantitative western blotting (Figure 4a-f), freeze-fracture immunogold labeling (Figure 3o-p, 9q), and DRM fractionation (Figure 9r). The convergence of multiple techniques strengthens this conclusion. This is a critical finding that distinguishes this model from caveolin KO models.

results.result: The presence of both caveolin3 and CAVIN-1 at the plasma membrane is insufficient for caveolar invagination in the absence of syndapin III. Despite unchanged levels of cav3 and CAVIN-1 at the plasma membrane in syndapin III KO cells, caveolar invaginations are severely impaired.
results.evaluation: Claims C3 and C51 are supported by the combination of data showing: (1) maintained cav3 and CAVIN-1 levels at the plasma membrane (C2, C41-C42, C45-C50), and (2) severe reduction in caveolar invaginations (C1, C34, C40). This represents a logical inference from well-supported observations. The conclusion challenges prior bacterial reconstitution studies (C99) and provides new mechanistic insight.

results.result: Syndapin III is crucial for caveolar invagination and localizes specifically to caveolar necks. Immunofluorescence showed high colocalization of syndapin III with cav3 at plasma membranes (Pearson coefficient 0.55±0.01). Freeze-fracture EM revealed 77% of syndapin III immunolabels were associated with membrane invaginations, and EM tomography demonstrated syndapin III localization at areas of membrane curvature transition from caveolar invagination to plasma membrane.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C29-C30, C36, C38, and C54 are well-supported by multiple high-resolution imaging techniques including immunofluorescence (Figure 1p-r), freeze-fracture EM (Figure 3a-c), and EM tomography with 3D reconstruction (Figure 5f-h, Videos 1-2). The localization data are quantitative and the tomography provides definitive 3D spatial information. The convergence of multiple imaging modalities at different resolutions strongly supports these claims.

results.result: Syndapin III KO renders cardiomyocytes sensitive to membrane tension. WT cardiomyocytes fully coped with moderate hypoosmotic stress (hypo30) and were only moderately affected by stronger stress (hypo15), while syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes showed significantly higher vulnerability under both conditions as measured by Trypan Blue assays.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C70-C71 are supported by quantitative Trypan Blue assays (Figure 8i-o) with 18 blinded experiments from six independent preparations. Statistical significance is demonstrated using one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-test. The experimental design includes appropriate controls (isoosmotic conditions) and two levels of stress. The blinded analysis strengthens the reliability of the findings.

results.result: Caveolae function as membrane tension buffers by flattening under mechanical stress. Hypoosmotic stress dramatically reduced deeply invaginated cav3-positive structures (~75%) in primary cardiomyocytes, while anti-cav3 labeling density at the plasma membrane remained constant, indicating redistribution rather than loss of caveolin3.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C66-C69 are supported by freeze-fracture EM analyses of cardiomyocytes and NIH3T3 cells under hypoosmotic stress (Figure 8a-h, Figure 8—figure supplement 1). The data show quantitative reduction in caveolar invaginations with maintained cav3 membrane association. This supports the membrane reservoir hypothesis. However, the inference that this represents the physiological role (C6) requires the additional context of exercise-induced pathology (C7) to be fully supported.

results.result: Syndapin III KO skeletal muscles show pathological parameters upon physical exercise similar to CAVEOLIN3 mutation-associated muscle diseases. Trained syndapin III KO mice displayed higher frequency of detached nuclei (about three times more frequent than WT), necrotic events demonstrated by acidic phosphatase staining, and inflammation. Training-induced hypertrophy was accompanied by increased rates of detached nuclei and necrosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C89-C91, and C95 are supported by comprehensive histological analyses (Figure 11) including H&E and acidic phosphatase staining. Quantitative data show statistically significant increases in detached nuclei (Figure 11g-h) with large sample sizes (WT untrained: 849 fibers; KO trained: 1244 fibers). The pathology is specifically exercise-induced, as untrained KO mice show minimal defects. This establishes physiological relevance of the caveolar defect.

results.result: Syndapin III forms membrane tubules with diameters matching caveolar dimensions. Both tagged and untagged full-length syndapin III formed tubules with average diameter of about 80 nm (range 75-90 nm), corresponding well to the 60-80 nm diameter of cav3-caveolae observed in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C53 are supported by two independent methods: freeze-fracture/TEM and cryo-TEM (Figure 5a-e). Quantitative diameter measurements (n=50 for GST-syndapin III, n=38 for syndapin III) show consistent results. The correspondence between in vitro tubule diameters and in vivo caveolar diameters supports a mechanistic role for syndapin III in membrane shaping. The use of both tagged and untagged protein controls for potential artifacts from the tag.

results.result: Syndapin III organizes caveolar coats and associated lipid environments. The syndapin III F-BAR domain interacts weakly with cav3 coats, and overexpression leads to cav3 colocalization at F-BAR-enriched sites. Cav3 and syndapin III float together in DRM preparations, but cav3 shows altered distribution upon syndapin III KO, shifting from fractions F4+F5 to F6+F7 in heart and from F3+F4 to F5+F6 in skeletal muscle.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C62 and C96 are supported by multiple biochemical approaches: coprecipitation (Figure 6a), immunofluorescence of overexpressed F-BAR domain (Figure 6b-c), and DRM fractionation (Figure 6d-i). The DRM shift is statistically significant (two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-test) with adequate sample sizes (heart n=3, skeletal muscle n=9 each genotype). The weak interaction (C56) is appropriately noted and compared to CAVIN-1. The convergence of multiple techniques supports the organizational role of syndapin III.

results.result: Syndapin III specifically associates with cav3-coated caveolae in muscle cells and not with cav1-coated caveolae from non-muscle cells. Cav1-coated caveolae in primary cell cultures were unaffected by syndapin III KO and remained normally invaginated.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C44 and C97 are supported by immunofluorescence and EM data (Figure 3—figure supplement 3). The specificity for cav3 over cav1 is demonstrated by: (1) no spatial overlap of cav1 and syndapin III in tissue sections, (2) presence of either cav1-labeled or syndapin III-labeled caveolae but not both in cardiomyocyte preparations, and (3) normal invagination of cav1-positive caveolae in syndapin III KO cells. This establishes isoform specificity and suggests different mechanisms for cav1 vs. cav3 caveolae formation.

results.result: CAVIN-1 membrane association and clustering is not impaired in syndapin III KO cells; instead, CAVIN-1 density at the plasma membrane moderately increased by about 30%. The CAVIN-1 density within clusters and the density of CAVIN-1 clusters both increased upon syndapin III KO.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C50 are supported by ultra-high-resolution freeze-fracture immunogold labeling (Figure 4g-k). Quantitative analyses show statistically significant increases in CAVIN-1 density (Figure 4i-k, p<0.01 and p<0.001). This finding contradicts previous reports using overexpressed CAVIN-1-mCherry in HeLa cells, but the current study uses endogenous protein in primary muscle cells with superior resolution. The authors appropriately note this discrepancy and suggest potential explanations.

results.result: Syndapin III KO does not affect ERK1/2 phosphorylation or dystrophin-glycoprotein complex localization and expression. Relative phosphoERK1/2 levels were unaltered, and no localization defects or expression changes of dystrophin and β-dystroglycan were detected in syndapin III KO muscles.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C65 are supported by quantitative immunoblotting (Figure 7a-b, g-j) and immunofluorescence (Figure 7c-f) with adequate sample sizes (n=12 each genotype). These negative results are important controls that distinguish the syndapin III KO phenotype from cav3 KO phenotypes reported in the literature. The data suggest that some cav3 KO phenotypes may reflect signaling defects rather than caveolar dysfunction per se.

results.result: Severe impairment of caveolar invagination in syndapin III KO hearts has no obvious cardiac consequences. Syndapin III KO mice showed no hypertrophic cardiac myocytes, unchanged heart/body weight ratios, normal left ventricle wall thickness, and no signs of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy or necrosis even at >64 weeks of age or after physical exercise. However, caveolar invagination was severely impaired in heart tissue (only 11.7% of WT caveolae remained).
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C79 are supported by multiple approaches: histology (Figure 9a-l), morphometric analyses (Figure 9c-h), and freeze-fracture EM (Figure 9m-p). Sample sizes are adequate (WT: 273 cells from 6 animals; KO: 378 cells from 7 animals for cardiomyocyte cross-sections). The lack of cardiac phenotype despite severe caveolar reduction is an important negative result that distinguishes caveolar function from caveolin function and suggests tissue-specific roles for caveolae.

results.result: Caveolar invagination is dramatically reduced in syndapin III KO skeletal muscle despite undisturbed cav3 presence at the plasma membrane. The density of deeply invaginated caveolae was dramatically reduced, and shallow cav3-positive indentations were strongly reduced. However, freeze-fractured skeletal muscles from syndapin III KO mice still showed about 70% of the cav3 cluster density observed in WT muscles, with only minor reduction (-7%) in cav3 density within persisting clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C88 are supported by comprehensive freeze-fracture EM analyses of skeletal muscle tissue (Figure 10o-p, s-t). The data show quantitative reductions in caveolar structures with statistical significance (two-tailed Student's t-test). The persistence of cav3 clusters despite loss of invaginations parallels findings in cardiomyocytes and further supports the conclusion that cav3 presence is insufficient for invagination. The quantitative nature of the data and large membrane areas analyzed (WT: 128 µm², KO: 69.2 µm²) strengthen these conclusions.

results.result: Untrained syndapin III KO muscles show altered fiber caliber spectrum with notable abundance of weakly established fibers. This increased abundance of fibers with small cross-sections was compensated by hypertrophy upon training.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C94 are supported by quantitative analyses of muscle fiber cross-sectional areas (Figure 11i-l) with large sample sizes (untrained WT: 849 fibers; untrained KO: 952 fibers; trained WT: 949 fibers; trained KO: 1244 fibers). The caliber spectrum analysis shows clear differences between genotypes, and the training-induced compensation is statistically significant (p<0.001 and p<0.01). However, the interpretation that this represents 'weakness' requiring compensation is somewhat inferential.

results.result: Syndapin III KO mice are viable, fertile, and develop without obvious impairments. Litter from heterozygous crosses showed normal Mendelian and gender distributions.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C28 are supported by observational data from the mouse colony (Figure 1l). The normal Mendelian ratios indicate no embryonic lethality, and normal gender distribution rules out sex-linked effects. This is an important baseline characterization showing that syndapin III is not essential for viability, unlike some other caveolar components.

results.result: Syndapin II expression levels remain unchanged in heart and skeletal muscles upon syndapin III KO, indicating no compensatory upregulation of this related family member.
results.evaluation: Claim C35 is supported by quantitative western blotting (Figure 2e-h) with adequate sample size (n=12 each genotype). This is an important control showing that the phenotype is specifically due to syndapin III loss and not compensated by the ubiquitously expressed syndapin II. The lack of syndapin I expression in muscle (C4, Figure 2d) further confirms specificity.

results.result: The density of shallow cav3-immunopositive indentations was unchanged upon syndapin III KO in cardiomyocytes, while deep invaginations were severely reduced.
results.evaluation: Claim C39 is supported by quantitative freeze-fracture EM analyses (Figure 3l) showing no significant change in shallow indentations. This differential effect on deep vs. shallow structures provides mechanistic insight into syndapin III function, suggesting it is specifically required for deep invagination rather than initial membrane deformation. However, this finding appears inconsistent with later data in heart tissue (C79) and skeletal muscle (C86) where shallow indentations were reduced, suggesting possible tissue-specific or context-dependent effects.

results.result: A significant portion of caveolae in muscle tissues are immunopositive for syndapin III. 3D rendering analyses showed that 32% of all cav3 spheres in skeletal muscle were positive for syndapin III.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 are supported by freeze-fracture EM (Figure 10c) and 3D rendering of confocal microscopy (Figure 10m-n). The finding that only ~32% of caveolae are syndapin III-positive at any given time, yet syndapin III KO causes dramatic reduction in all caveolae, suggests a dynamic or catalytic role for syndapin III rather than being a stable structural component. This is consistent with the weak interaction with cav3 (C56).

results.result: Muscular caveolar invaginations are largely dispensable for life but help preserve muscle cells from abrupt tear forces. When caveolae as membrane tension compensators are impaired, physical exercise-inducible hypertrophy is counterproductive to compensate muscle fiber weakness.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C105 represent high-level interpretations of the collective data. C103 is supported by the viability of syndapin III KO mice (C27) and comparison to cav3 KO literature. C104 is inferred from the exercise-induced pathology (C7, C89-C91) and osmotic stress sensitivity (C5, C71). C105 is inferred from the observation that training induces hypertrophy (C94) accompanied by increased pathology (C95). These are reasonable interpretations but represent inferences beyond the direct data. The conclusion about hypertrophy being 'counterproductive' is somewhat speculative.

results.result: Background claims about caveolae, caveolins, and related proteins from the literature. These include historical information, established knowledge about caveolar structure and composition, prior findings from caveolin KO studies, human disease associations, and previous work on syndapin II and CAVIN-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C26 and C98-C102 are literature-based claims supported by appropriate citations. These provide essential context for interpreting the current findings. The authors accurately represent prior work, including contradictory findings (e.g., C15 vs. C16 on cav3 KO heart phenotypes). The citations appear appropriate and the claims are consistent with established knowledge in the field. These background claims are important for framing the novelty and significance of the current work.
